notable.name: Swedish
notable.note: co-official nationally; small native-speaker minority, bilingual signage common on the west/south coast

notable.name: Sámi languages
notable.note: official status in the northernmost municipalities (Lapland)

terrainDescription.zh: 國土大部分覆蓋北方針葉林與數萬座湖泊，地勢平緩，南部與西部沿海有較集中的農業帶。
terrainDescription.en: Mostly covered by boreal taiga forest and tens of thousands of lakes, with gentle terrain and a more concentrated agricultural belt along the south/west coast.

plate.color: white background, black text, blue EU band with oval "FIN" on the left

roadInfra.bollardStyle: Cylindrical black-and-white bollard — the black portion contains a white rectangle; a shape not shared with the other Nordic countries' bollards

utilityPole.transformerMount: Simple wooden poles with varying pole-top styles; lamps are normally double-bolted to the top of the pole; orange snow poles with a thin white band near the top are common roadside markers (Norway/Sweden also use snow poles, but with a much wider, lower-set white band — a useful Finland-vs-Norway/Sweden differentiator)

historicalContext.zh: 芬蘭語屬烏拉爾語系（芬蘭-烏戈爾語族），與北歐鄰國（挪威、瑞典、丹麥）所屬的北日耳曼語族完全無關，是「北歐地理分組」不等於「語言親緣關係」的鮮明案例；瑞典語為全國共同官方語言，西部與南部沿海地區常見芬蘭語／瑞典語雙語路牌。
historicalContext.en: Finnish belongs to the Uralic (Finno-Ugric) language family, completely unrelated to the North Germanic languages of its Nordic neighbors (Norway, Sweden, Denmark) — a clear case where geographic "Nordic" grouping doesn't imply linguistic kinship. Swedish is co-official nationwide, and bilingual Finnish/Swedish road signage is common along the west and south coasts.
